data.text:
Nakakabahala na talaga how flood control projects in the Philippines are being handled. For so many years, we’ve seen the same scenario billions allocated by DPWH, multiple projects announced left and right, pero every rainy season, it’s still the same story: binabaha pa rin tayo.

As taxpayers, we give our hard-earned money with the hope na these projects will finally address the problem. Pero ang nakikita natin? Half-baked infrastructures, substandard materials, or projects na hindi natatapos on time. Tapos after a while, masisira ulit, and then another budget is proposed na naman. It’s like a never-ending cycle of inefficiency at the expense of ordinary Filipinos.

Mas lalo pang nakakasama ng loob kapag nalalaman natin na may mga contractor na hindi lang kumikita ng sobra, kundi ginagamit pa ang pera ng taumbayan para sa sariling luho. May isang contractor pa nga na nakabili ng 28 luxury cars kasama ang isang Rolls Royce at ang dahilan niya? Dahil lang daw sa payong feature sa pinto ng sasakyan. Like seriously? Habang milyon-milyon ang Pilipino lumulubog sa baha, eto yung dahilan kung bakit ginastos ang perang dapat nakalaan para sa flood control. That’s not just corruption, that’s pure insult to the Filipino people.

And let’s take note hindi lang flood control projects ang usapan dito. If ganito ang klase ng corruption na nangyayari sa infrastructure, paano pa kaya sa healthcare at education? What if pera na dapat para sa ospital, gamot, public health workers, at scholarship programs nauuwi lang din sa luho ng iilang tao? Nakakatakot isipin na ang perang pinaghihirapan ng ordinaryong taxpayers ay nauuwi lang sa pagbili ng sasakyan na may payong feature, instead of services that could save lives and build a better future.

Because at the end of the day, corruption doesn’t just waste money it steals safety, opportunity, and dignity. Every project na hindi maayos ang gawa means more families losing homes to floods, more children wading through baha to get to school, and more communities left vulnerable. It’s a betrayal to the very people who fund these projects tayong mga taxpayers.

Public service should never be treated like a business deal. Infrastructure projects should prioritize quality and transparency, not kickbacks and profit. Accountability is not optional it’s a responsibility. Ang bawat piso na binabayad natin in taxes should come back to us in the form of genuine, lasting improvements, not in luxury cars and excuses as shallow as a “payong sa pinto ng kotse.”

At sana maalala ng mga namumuno at gumagawa ng mga project na ito: The Filipino people are not asking for luxury, only for honesty. Hindi sobra-sobra ang hinihiling ng bayan, kundi ang karapat-dapat lang na serbisyo at proyekto na may saysay. Hindi namin kailangang makita ng contractors na nagcocollect ng ibat-ibang luxury cars ang gusto naming makita ay kalsadang hindi binabaha at pamilyang ligtas sa sakuna!
